description: O(N*M) allocations in string-rindex due to substring in a loop. For large stdout, this creates thousands of temporary strings, causing significant GC pressure.
code_snippet:
(let loop ([i (- hlen nlen)])
            (cond
             [(< i 0) #f]
             [(string=? (substring haystack i (+ i nlen)) needle) i]
             [else (loop (- i 1))]))
suggested_fix: Use a character-by-character comparison or a native string search function (like string-contains or string-index) to avoid O(N) allocations in the search loop.

description: O(N*M) allocations in string-search due to substring in a loop. LLM responses can be large, making this a significant bottleneck during response parsing.
code_snippet:
(let loop ([i 0])
            (cond
             [(> (+ i nlen) hlen) #f]
             [(string=? (substring haystack i (+ i nlen)) needle) i]
             [else (loop (+ i 1))]))
suggested_fix: Implement string searching using character indices and char=? instead of allocating new substrings for every comparison.

description: Sequential execution of models in run-parallel-council. Despite being named 'parallel', it calls LLMs one by one, multiplying latency by the number of models.
code_snippet:
;;; Get all responses in parallel (sequentially for now)
       (let loop ([remaining models]
                  [responses '()])
suggested_fix: Implement true parallel execution using threads or async tasks if the Scheme environment supports it, allowing multiple LLM requests to be in flight simultaneously.

description: Blocking input handling in a UI/animation loop. The call to get-line blocks the entire heartbeat, preventing animations and particle updates from occurring unless the user is typing.
suggested_fix: Use non-blocking IO (char-ready?) or a separate thread for input to allow the animation loop to tick and render independently of user interaction.

description: Redundant O(N) pinning operation in save-duckie!. Every state update (like petting) re-pins all existing memories, which likely involves disk IO or database updates.
code_snippet:
(define (save-duckie! d)
  (let* ([blk (duckie->block d)]
         [hash (store! blk)])
        (pin! hash)
        ;; Also pin all memory hashes
        (for-each pin! (duckie-memories d))
        hash))
suggested_fix: Only pin the new DUCKIE state hash. Memories should be pinned once when they are created (in remember!) rather than repeatedly during every soul update.

description: O(N^2) total complexity in state merging due to list appends. As pipelines grow or nest, repeatedly appending log and artifact lists becomes increasingly expensive.
code_snippet:
(define (merge-states parent child)
  (make-pipeline-state
   (append (state-log child) (state-log parent))
   (append (state-artifacts child) (state-artifacts parent))
suggested_fix: Use a more efficient structure for logs/artifacts, such as a nested list (dlist) or a trie, and only flatten/linearize the results at the end of the pipeline execution.
